title: Machine Learning Systems

items.front: What’s the difference between overfitting and underfitting?
items.hook: Your model’s either a genius or a dummy.

items.front: What’s a simple way to prevent overfitting?
items.hook: Keep your model on a leash.

items.front: What’s the purpose of a validation set?
items.hook: Your model’s practice test, no peeking.

items.front: What’s the difference between batch and stochastic gradient descent?
items.back: Batch uses all data, stochastic uses one sample.
items.hook: One’s a crowd, one’s a loner.

items.front: What’s a confusion matrix used for?
items.hook: True or false, but make it fancy.

items.back: Data gets sparse in high dimensions.

items.text: The first neural network was inspired by the human brain in 1943.
Deep learning models can have over 175 billion parameters.
Machine learning can predict your personality just from your Spotify playlists.

items.title: Why Do We Even Need This?

quiz.explain: Overfitting happens when the model is too complex, leading to low bias and high variance.
L2 regularization adds the squared magnitude of weights to the loss function.

quiz.q: When do you use the validation set?
quiz.explain: The validation set is used to adjust hyperparameters before final testing.

quiz.q: Which is more computationally expensive per iteration?
quiz.explain: Batch Gradient Descent uses the entire dataset in each iteration, making it more expensive.

quiz.q: Which metric is calculated as TP / (TP + FP)?
quiz.explain: Precision measures the accuracy of positive predictions.
Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a common dimensionality reduction technique.

quiz.q: Who proposed the first neural network model?
quiz.explain: McCulloch and Pitts created the first computational model of a neural network in 1943.

quiz.q: Which model holds the record for the largest number of parameters?
quiz.explain: Megatron-LM, developed by NVIDIA and Microsoft, has over 530 billion parameters.

quiz.q: Which personality trait is most strongly linked to music preferences?
quiz.explain: Openness to Experience is most strongly correlated with diverse music tastes.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Alright, imagine your phone predicts your next word before you type it. That’s machine learning in action!

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: So, my phone’s spying on me and guessing I’ll say ‘pizza’ next?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Not spying—learning! It studies patterns in what you’ve typed before.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Great, so now my phone thinks I’m a pizza-obsessed maniac.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Exactly! It’s just recognizing trends, not judging your life choices.

quiz_after.q: What’s the core idea behind machine learning?
quiz_after.reaction_correct: Wow, you’re smarter than my phone.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Ever hear of supervised learning? It’s like training a dog with treats.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: So, my data gets a biscuit every time it does a good job?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Close! You give it labeled data—like ‘this is a cat’—to learn from.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: And unsupervised? No treats?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: No labels. It finds patterns on its own, like grouping similar data.

quiz_after.q: What’s the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning?
options: One uses treats, the other doesn’t
One uses labeled data, the other doesn’t
One is for cats, the other for dogs
quiz_after.reaction_wrong: Nope, but at least you tried.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Neural networks are like a web of brain cells, but for your computer.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: So my laptop’s growing neurons now?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Not growing—mimicking! Layers of nodes process data like neurons do.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Cool, so my computer’s about to develop a personality disorder.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Not yet, but give it time.

segments.title: Why Do We Even Need This?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Machine learning powers things like fraud detection and recommendations.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: So Netflix knows I’ll binge-watch bad 80s movies?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Yep! It learns what you like and suggests more of it.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: But what if I don’t want it to know that?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: That’s the trade-off: convenience vs. privacy.

quiz_after.q: What’s a common use of machine learning?
quiz_after.reaction_correct: Bingo! Now go watch some 80s movies.
quiz_after.reaction_wrong: Nope, but fraud detection *would* catch that.
